The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts

Jun Du

While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

Carl Court/Getty Images

Nov 18, 2026
5 min read

MANCHESTER—Now that protectionism is back, understanding the full costs and knock-on effects of trade barriers has become imperative for governments navigating a more uncertain global economy. The United Kingdom’s experience after leaving the European Union is especially revealing in this respect, because Brexit reduced both the value of UK goods exports to the EU as well as the number of different products sold there. While much of the post-Brexit debate has focused on the first cost, the second one warrants more attention, especially now that the UK and the EU are preparing for a delayed summit on resetting their relationship.
